extracted.intended_audience: literate public interested in morals, theatre, and conduct (readers of The Spectator)
extracted.subtask_description: Short moral and critical guidance about English comedy, stage conduct, and personal virtue intended to evaluate and improve theatre, social behaviour, and character. Primarily addresses playwrights, audiences, and citizens on suitable subjects, portrayal, and private conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre should promote virtue and improve behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Were our English Stage but half so virtuous as that of the Greeks or Romans, we should quickly see the Influence of it in the Behaviour of all the Politer Part of Mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stage ought to recommend religion, government, and public worship; it should not be fashionable to ridicule religion, nor make the man of pleasure the compleat gentleman. Good theatre contributes to the 'Accomplishment and Refining of Human Nature' and should leave audiences wiser and better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject choice: avoid improper topics for ridicule
rubrics_metrics.description: There was another Rule likewise, which was observed by Authors of Antiquity...and that was never to chuse an improper Subject for Ridicule. Now a Subject is improper for Ridicule, if it is apt to stir up Horrour and Commiseration rather than Laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not base comedy on subjects that naturally move pity or horror (e.g., incest, murder). Ancient models (Terence, etc.) avoided raising laughter from such crimes; choosing these subjects for ridicule is a moral and artistic error.

rubrics_metrics.name: When representing vice, mark it as blameworthy (no glamorizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever Vices are represented upon the Stage, they ought to be so marked and branded by the Poet, as not to appear either laudable or amiable in the Person who is tainted with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a character displays immoral behaviour, the drama should make it clear that such behaviour is not admirable; do not contrive matters so that the criminals become the favourites of the audience. Avoid plotting so that immoral characters win audience sympathy without condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making immoral characters the audience's favourites
rubrics_metrics.description: At the same time the Poet so contrives Matters, that the two Criminals are the Favourites of the Audience... The accomplished Gentleman upon the English Stage, is the Person that is familiar with other Men's Wives, and indifferent to his own; as the fine Woman is generally a Composition of Sprightliness and Falshood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not portray adultery, cuckoldry, or libertinism as the mark of the 'fine' gentleman or woman; avoid stylising vice as wit or amiable sprightliness. Strive to present virtuous fine characters rather than defaulting to virulent stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage should be subject to proper inspections and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the English Stage were under the same Regulations the Athenian was formerly, it would have the same Effect... Were our Plays subject to proper Inspections and Limitations, we might not only pass away several of our vacant Hours in the highest Entertainments; but should always rise from them wiser and better than we sat down to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation or censorship (properly applied) is proposed as a means to restrain licentiousness and make theatre contribute to morality; the objective is wholesome entertainment that refines, not corrupts, public taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not choose low or indecent subjects merely to comply with corrupt taste
rubrics_metrics.description: When Persons of a low Genius attempt this kind of Writing, they know no difference between being Merry and being Lewd...they complied with the corrupt Taste of the more Vicious Part of their Audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pandering to the vicious parts of the audience by trading wit for lewdness; writers of 'low genius' confuse merriment with lewdness. Artistic standards require discernment between true humour and base indecency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom/habit shapes character; choose an excellent course and persist
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimum vitæ genus eligito, nam consuetudo faciet jucundissimum. Pitch upon that Course of Life which is the most Excellent, and Custom will render it the most Delightful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because habit converts actions into pleasures, one should select a life guided by reason and excellence; steady practice converts duty and virtuous labour into delight. Useful for advising personal conduct and for moral didacticism in literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual practice of virtue creates dispositions fit for heavenly happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Practice of Religion will not only be attended with that Pleasure...but with those Supernumerary Joys of Heart...The Seeds of those spiritual Joys...must be planted in her, during this her present State of Probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument that moral education and repeated virtuous acts are necessary to form the soul for future beatitude; conversely, long custom in vice prepares men for misery. Use this to justify moral instruction and virtuous character portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep promises (even small ones); small breaches undermine integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a certain frivolous Falshood that People indulge themselves in, which ought to be had in greater Detestation than it commonly meets with: What I mean is a Neglect of Promises made on small and indifferent Occasions...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to keep trivial appointments or promises breeds distrust and damages a man's honesty as surely as perjury; habitual lateness or careless promises erode social credit and moral character. Writers and moralists should treat small duties as formative of integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid promising to please or to display vanity; be cautious in accepting/issuing invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: This Fault is sometimes to be accounted for, when desirable People are fearful of appearing precious and reserved by Denials; but they will find the Apprehension of that Imputation will betray them into a childish Impotence of Mind, and make them promise all who are so kind to ask it of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make promises from vanity or fear of seeming proud; false engagements to please others lead to ingratitude and habitual breaking of one's word. Better to decline than to create habitual dishonesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray female virtue: filial piety and domestic devotion (Fidelia model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fidelia...employs her whole Time in Care and Attendance upon her Father...she will not marry during his Life...Her filial Regard to him is what she makes her Diversion, her Business, and her Glory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal female character combines accomplishments (music, reading, conversation) with devoted domestic duty and self-restraint in love; such models are proposed as patterns for writing virtuous women and for social emulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social entertainments should foster decent conversation and moral discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: There are at his House in the most regular Order, Assemblies of People of the highest Merit; where there is Conversation without Mention of the Faults of the Absent, Benevolence between Men and Women without Passion, and the highest Subjects of Morality treated of as natural and accidental Discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemblies and entertainments ought to be ordered so as to encourage benevolence and moral topics rather than slander, passion, or base amusements; useful guidance for portrayals of social scenes and prescriptions for civility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of money's moral influence: security vs. corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Money...has got the upper Hand of what all Mankind formerly thought most dear, viz. Security; and I wish I could say she had here put a Stop to her Victories; but, alas! common Honesty fell a Sacrifice to her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Money provides supports in calamity and can foster piety and devotion, but the love of money can overpower other virtues and lead to moral corruption. When evaluating behaviour or constructing characters, acknowledge both the stabilizing and corrosive effects of wealth.
